reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(argument-1), argument-1 a positive integer counting days after 1600-12-31 (A.2.13.3 AR1, no upper bound in the 1989 module), returns the Julian date of that same day: the year and day of year the day count lands on in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window sig.IntroducedIn (85) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel: DAY-OF-INTEGER is admitted at 85

DialectBehaviors.IsActive(DialectBehavior.IntegerDateFormBounded, year): inactive at 85, so BoundIntrinsicCall.IntegerDateFormUnbounded = true and the renderer passes unbounded: true to CobolDate.DayOfInteger (no 3,067,671 cap)
Constructs.NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: an integer function written outside an arithmetic expression (DISPLAY FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(1)) is refused at 85, as A.2.3 (3) requires

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, CobolDate.cs and DialectBehavior.cs for Edition, DialectLevel, DialectBehavior, ConstructRegistry; the day arithmetic (YearAndDayOf) has no edition input.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an argument past 3,067,671 (9999-12-31) is still a positive integer and returns its Julian date (3067672 -> 10000001, 4382911 -> 13601001); at 2023 the same arguments return 0 (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION default).

reader.notes: The 1985 run takes its own arm (unbounded integer date form) and that arm matches the 1989 module's text, which bounds the day count only below. Every probed day converts to the right year and day of year, including century and 400-year boundaries and days past 9999. The brief's citation form §1985:A.2.13.4 fails cite.py (Section A is X3.23a-1989), so the catalog's §1989 form is used.
